title: How Much Does a Teaspoon of NEUTRON Star Weigh? 🥄
description:
How much does a teaspoon of neutron star weigh? About as much as a mountain: NASA puts a sugar cube or a teaspoon of it at roughly a billion tonnes here on Earth. A neutron star packs more than our Sun's mass (usually about 1.4 Suns) into a ball about 20 km across, the size of a city. Atoms are mostly empty space, and that crush squeezes the empty space out, so its stuff is packed as tight as the middle of an atom. And if you brought a spoonful home, it wouldn't stay in the spoon: without its star's gravity holding it in, it would spring apart with an enormous blast. One spoon or two?
